mechanism_narrative: The current level of real GDP (GDPC1) serves as a direct proxy for aggregate economic activity; higher GDP levels consistently correlate with stronger corporate earnings and consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of cyclical phase.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 exceeds its 5-year moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in unemployment rate above 6.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer confidence and corporate hiring, which directly causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 6.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in consumer spending (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates robust aggregate demand; their joint increase creates a multiplicative effect on corporate revenue visibility, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction effect fails to predict positive returns in more than 60% of cases when both RSAFS and HOUST exceed thresholds, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: High industrial production growth (INDPRO > 105.0) signals expanding manufacturing capacity and rising corporate output, which directly boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days during early economic expansions.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO exceeds 105.0.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 1.5% indicates active monetary tightening, increasing borrowing costs for corporations and reducing equity valuation multiples, which directly causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 1.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent employment growth (PAYEMS > 136000) and declining unemployment (UNRATE < 6.6) indicate a tightening labor market, which increases consumer spending power and corporate profit margins, creating a multiplicative positive effect on S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction effect fails to predict positive returns in more than 60% of cases when both conditions are met, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 1.0% during stable inflation environments indicates accommodative monetary policy, reducing discount rates for equity cash flows and supporting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days in early easing cycles.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 1.0%.

mechanism_narrative: The current level of employment (PAYEMS) consistently reflects labor market strength; higher employment levels directly correlate with increased consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of cyclical context.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS exceeds its 12-month moving average.
